R744.note: Replaces format()-as-XSS-and-format-string sink with Encode.forHtml()+print, dropping the format-args usage entirely, which is required to remove both the XSS and the format-string issue and matches the case's simple echo intent.

R745.note: Allowlist pattern is the correct shape for an ORDER BY identifier, but it replaces whatever raw sort values callers previously sent with new invented keys (id_asc, id_desc, ...); this input-contract change is explained but not flagged as a compatibility break for existing callers.

R746.note: Adds the missing offset>=0 check exactly as needed; valid/invalid behavior matches the stated contract.

R747.note: Correct golang-jwt v5 pattern: type-asserts token.Method plus jwt.WithValidMethods; closes the algorithm-confusion vector without changing behavior for legitimate RS256 tokens.

R748.note: Compile-verified failure: 'bytes' is imported but never used and 'header' from r.FormFile is declared but never used (confirmed with go build), so the file as written will not compile even though the content-sniffing/random-filename/path-containment design is otherwise sound and its behavior changes (random filename returned, MaxBytesReader, O_EXCL) are disclosed.

R749.note: Bounds check before the write satisfies the contract's 'rejected or reported' requirement for invalid slots; struct/API otherwise unchanged.

R750.note: Switching to the tarfile module eliminates CLI option parsing entirely, so a leading '-' can never be read as a tar flag; archiving behavior for normal filenames is preserved.

R751.note: Allowlisting the executable name closes the arbitrary-binary-execution vector while keeping the documented ping/traceroute/nslookup use cases working.

R752.note: The primary fix reuses DOMPurify.sanitize(..., ALLOWED_TAGS: []) for the title attribute, which strips tags but does not encode quote characters, so the attribute-breakout described in the write-up's own Explanation is still exploitable; a correct HTML-attribute-escaping helper is only offered as a third, 'Or simplest' alternative rather than as the fix.

R753.note: random_bytes(16)+bin2hex is a standard CSPRNG token replacement; drops the unused client_nonce cleanly with no other side effects.

R754.note: Swapping text/template for html/template is the minimal, correct, drop-in fix; template and data contract are unchanged.

R755.note: Canonicalizing the base dir and requiring an exact match or a separator-bounded prefix correctly closes the sibling-directory bypass without altering valid-file behavior.

R756.note: Pre-checks combined length before strncat, matching the original construction and rejection logic exactly except for the timing of the bounds check.

R757.note: Column/direction allowlists match the actual SELECT columns and preserve accountId parameterization and the default sort.

R758.note: Uses the documented ASP.NET Core minimal-API pattern (IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync plus UseAntiforgery) required for JSON-bound endpoints; matches Microsoft's own sample and preserves the 202/QueueAsync path for valid tokens.

R759.note: Uses the four-arg DirContext.search overload with a {0} placeholder and filterArgs, which JNDI escapes per RFC 2254; new SearchControls() is documented as equivalent to the original null argument, so search behavior is unchanged.

R760.note: %s placeholder plus repr() escapes embedded CR/LF so injected control characters can't forge log lines; the added quoting/escaping is disclosed and doesn't affect the login flow.

R761.note: Adds the missing mode != NULL short-circuit check exactly matching the required strict/other/unset behavior.

R762.note: Bounds check before the array write silently drops out-of-range packets, consistent with the function's existing void/no-error-reporting signature.

R763.note: execFile with an argument array removes shell metacharacter injection, and the added leading-'-' rejection closes the argument-injection gap that a bare argument array alone would leave open.
